title: Measurement Word Problems: Length, Time, Liquid Volume, Mass and Money
seo_title: Grade 4 Measurement Word Problems Worksheets (TEKS 4.8C, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.8C solve problems that deal with measurements of length, intervals of time, liquid volumes, mass, and money using addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division as appropriate
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 measurement word problem worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.8C: length, elapsed time, liquid volume, mass and money problems with all four operations. 100 STAAR-style questions with answers.
key_big: Use the same unit for every number, then choose the operation.
key_sub: 1 hour = 60 minutes, 1 foot = 12 inches, 1 liter = 1,000 milliliters.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Read what is measured: length, time, liquid volume, mass or money. Decide whether to add, subtract, multiply or divide.
  • Make the units the same before you compute: 2 feet 5 inches = 29 inches; 3 liters = 3,000 milliliters.
  • For time, 1 hour = 60 minutes. Count to the next hour, then add the rest.

Examples

Example

Practice starts at 3:40 p.m. and lasts 55 minutes. When does it end?

3:40 + 20 minutes = 4:00

4:00 + 35 minutes = 4:35

Answer: 4:35 p.m.

Example

How many 250 mL cups can be filled from 2 liters?

2 L = 2,000 mL

2,000 ÷ 250 = 8

Answer: 8 cups

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Computing with different unitsConvert first so both numbers use the same unit.
Treating an hour as 100 minutes1 hour = 60 minutes.
Choosing the wrong operationAsk: are amounts joined, compared, repeated or shared?

faq.a: Solve problems that deal with measurements of length, intervals of time, liquid volumes, mass and money using addition, subtraction, multiplication or division as appropriate.

faq.q: Do I need to convert units?
faq.a: Often, yes. Change to the same unit before you add or subtract.

faq.q: How do I solve elapsed time problems?
faq.a: Count forward to the next hour, then add the rest of the minutes.

faq.q: How do I work with money?
faq.a: Line up the decimal points to add or subtract, and remember that $1 = 100 cents.

items.e: Add 1 hour: 7:45 p.m. Add 50 minutes: 15 minutes gets to 8:00, then 35 more minutes is 8:35 p.m.

items.q: Zoe's soccer practice starts at 3:40 p.m. and ends at 5:15 p.m. How long is practice?
items.e: From 3:40 to 4:40 is 1 hour. From 4:40 to 5:00 is 20 minutes, and 5:00 to 5:15 is 15 minutes. 1 hr + 20 min + 15 min = 1 hr 35 min.

items.q: A relay race is 2 km long. Four runners each run the same distance. How many meters does each runner run?
items.e: 2 km = 2,000 m. Share it equally: 2,000 ÷ 4 = 500 m.

items.q: A bag has 2 kg of flour. A baker uses 750 g. How many grams of flour are left?
items.e: Use the same unit: 2 kg = 2,000 g. Then subtract: 2,000 − 750 = 1,250 g.

items.q: Emma reads for 12 hour on Monday and 14 hour on Tuesday. How many minutes does she read in all?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30, and one fourth of 60 is 15. In all: 30 + 15 = 45 minutes.

items.q: Pencils cost 45 cents each. Mia buys 6 pencils. How much does she pay?
A pitcher holds 3 L of lemonade. How many 500 mL bottles can be filled from the pitcher?
items.e: 3 L = 3,000 mL. How many groups of 500 mL are in 3,000 mL? 3,000 ÷ 500 = 6 bottles.

items.q: Harper has a rope that is 3 m long. She cuts off 85 cm. How long is the rope now?
items.e: Use the same unit: 3 m = 300 cm. The rope gets shorter, so subtract: 300 − 85 = 215 cm.

items.q: Luis has $5.00. He buys a juice for $1.35 and a muffin for $2.40. How much change does he get?
A bag holds 8 apples. Each apple has a mass of 150 g. What is the mass of all the apples?
Four friends share the cost of an $18.00 pizza equally. How much does each friend pay?
items.e: Share equally, so divide: $18.00 ÷ 4. 18 ÷ 4 = 4 with 2 dollars left over. 2 dollars = 200 cents, and 200 ÷ 4 = 50 cents. Each friend pays $4.50 (not $4.20).

items.q: Carlos needs 5 yards of ribbon. He has 12 feet of ribbon. How many more feet does he need?
items.e: 5 yd = 5 × 3 = 15 ft. Find the missing part: 15 − 12 = 3 ft.

items.q: A recipe needs 1 pound of cheese. Caleb has 10 ounces. How many more ounces does he need?
items.e: 1 lb = 16 oz. Find the missing part: 16 − 10 = 6 oz.

items.q: A family drives for 3 hours on Saturday and 2 12 hours on Sunday. How many minutes do they drive in all?
items.e: Saturday: 3 × 60 = 180 min. Sunday: 2 × 60 = 120 min, plus 12 hour = 30 min, so 150 min. In all: 180 + 150 = 330 minutes.

items.q: Lucia runs 3 km and then walks 450 m. How many meters does she go in all?
A bean plant grows for 3 weeks and 4 days. How many days is that?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days, so 3 weeks = 21 days. Add the leftover 4 days: 21 + 4 = 25 days.

items.q: A song is 3 minutes 25 seconds long. Noah plays it 2 times. How many seconds is that?
items.e: 3 min = 3 × 60 = 180 sec, so the song is 180 + 25 = 205 seconds. 2 times: 2 × 205 = 410 seconds.

items.q: Mateo has a board that is 6 feet long. He cuts it into pieces that are 8 inches long. How many pieces does he get?
items.e: 6 ft = 6 × 12 = 72 in. How many 8-inch pieces are in 72 inches? 72 ÷ 8 = 9 pieces.

items.q: A 2 L bottle of water costs $1.80. A 500 mL bottle costs $0.65. Marcus needs 2 L of water. How much does he save by buying the 2 L bottle instead of 500 mL bottles?
Isaac drinks 3 glasses of milk every day. Each glass holds 250 mL. How much milk does he drink in 1 week?
items.e: One day: 3 × 250 = 750 mL. 1 week = 7 days, so 7 × 750 = 5,250 mL.
